To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the more a follower perceives that a leader acts ethically, and in a way that the follower expects, the more trust the follower has in their leader.

(a) the ethical leadership behaviors of role modeling, demonstrating moral integrity, contextualizing success and transmitting organizational values are positively related to the trust that followers have in their leaders, (b) the ethical leadership behavior of encouraging transparency is not significantly related to trust, (c) the ethical leadership of securing ethical behavior is negatively related to trust, and (d) the relationship between ethical leadership behavior and trust is moderated by the consistency of that ethical leadership behavior with the expectations that followers have for a leader

(1) ethical leadership is a multidimensional concept; (2) different ethical leadership behaviors are positively related with trust; and (3) the relationship between ethical leadership and trust is partly mediated by the consistency between the desired and the observed ethical leadership behaviors, perceived by followers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what is the relationship between different ethical leader behaviors and trust?
the effects of ethical leader behaviors on the trust that followers have in their leaders.

the relationship between ethical leadership and trust, and we find that this relationship is not only a positive one, but that it is also partly moderated by the consistency of leader behavior as perceived by the followers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ethical leadership is about meeting the expectations of followers.
the more a follower perceives that a leader acts in an ethical manner, the more that follower will trust the leader.
ethical leadership is a key driver of trust, and the more a leader behaves ethically, the more trust will be created.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trust is a result of the extent to which a leader meets the expectations of their followers.
trust is a function of the extent to which followers perceive that a leader is behaving in a manner that meets their expectations of what an ethical leader is.
ethical leadership is not about what leaders do, but about how leaders behave. It is all about meeting expectations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trust is based on the perception that a leader acts in an appropriate manner, and not just on the fact that a leader does good things.
trust in leaders is based on the expectations followers have of a leader.
leaders need to understand what followers expect of them as ethical leaders. If they do not meet these expectations, trust is at risk.
